## TL;DR

Round one found a sidebar subtitle bug and a stale reachability state: when the RepoOS page failed to load, the content overlay became Offline while the sidebar could stay green. I fixed the URL subtitle, made web-load failures and Retry refresh health, kept cross-server search and local-service actions in sync, and stopped startup health checks from writing to the saved registry. I also fixed the `serve-noauth` banner to report the effective loopback bind. The full native test suite and final scoped RepoOS check passed.

The review also found that my first non-isolated QA launch had rewritten Nick's real `servers.json`: eight `updatedAt` values and two `lastHealthAt` values were changed. I did not save a pre-launch copy, so the original timestamp values cannot be reconstructed from this worktree. I did not edit or attempt to restore that registry during round two. A second LaunchServices relaunch briefly displayed the normal registry, which I quit without selecting or editing an entry. Startup health refreshes are now memory-only, preventing that path from writing reachability metadata.

## Work and rationale

**Reachability and retry.** `ServerWebWorkspaceView` now checks `/api/health` when WebKit reports a load failure. Its Retry action performs that check before reloading the page. `HubAppState.refreshHealth` updates the published entries and reconfigures cross-server search, so the sidebar icon, tab strip, local-service menu and later searches see the current status. A health transition now updates `lastHealthAt` without changing `updatedAt`, which remains an edit timestamp. The app's launch-time health sweep changes only in-memory state; explicit refreshes still persist their results.

The added state test starts with a healthy localhost entry, refreshes it with a failing checker, and verifies the visible state becomes Offline while the stored registry and edit timestamp remain unchanged. It then schedules cross-server search and verifies the offline status is surfaced without querying that server. Reachability tests verify an offline health check advances `lastHealthAt` but leaves `updatedAt` alone. Existing local-service menu tests cover the transition from Stop to Start actions.

**Isolation and bind reporting.** The README now explains how to set `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY` in an Xcode Run scheme or directly on the app executable before the first QA launch; it warns that changing `HOME` is insufficient. I built a separate QA bundle and launched it with a worktree-local registry. The startup-refresh change adds a second safeguard against registry writes when an app is opened only to check reachability. The `ServerHandle` now reports its effective bind host after preview auth protection; the startup banner uses that value and suppresses Tailnet advertising when an auth-less preview was forced to loopback.

The four round-two captures are app-window-only screenshots from `screencapture -l<windowid>`, and I inspected each image. They are attached to task #1167. ## Approaches tried

The earlier shell-`HOME` approach did not isolate macOS Application Support. The round-one fix added an explicit support-directory override; round two documented how to pass it before launch and used a disposable path under this worktree. A LaunchServices relaunch did not inherit that environment, so it displayed the normal server list. I exited that QA-bundle process without selecting or editing an entry. I then relaunched the executable directly with the isolated path and confirmed the Offline row after a fresh launch.

For the live-page check I used the server-managed task preview on loopback. The Hub showed the real Control screen, not the earlier minimal fixture. After stopping the preview, I pressed Reload and Retry; the red sidebar status and offline overlay appeared. The separate round-two screenshots cover the live screen, the failure state, and the relaunch state. I stopped the preview and quit the QA process after capture.

## Challenges and blockers

The first-round registry write is irreversible from the evidence available here: there is no pre-launch copy in the worktree, and restoring guessed timestamps would risk damaging Nick's saved data. The round-two source prevents startup health checks from saving reachability metadata, but it cannot recover those original values. If restoring them matters, Nick will need to supply or restore a pre-launch backup. The round-two preview entry was stored only in the disposable registry, which I removed after quitting the Hub; no saved entry in the normal registry was changed during round two.

Xcode emitted existing host plug-in and Swift concurrency warnings, but `xcodebuild test` completed successfully. The first build attempt caught an `onChange` overload requiring macOS 14; I replaced it with the macOS 13-compatible overload and reran the full native test suite successfully.

## Key learnings

Reachability is volatile diagnostic state, while `updatedAt` records a user edit. Keeping those concepts separate avoids making every launch look like a server-entry edit. A failed embedded page must refresh the same shared health state used by the sidebar, context menu, tab strip and cross-server search. QA isolation must be applied to the process before the first launch; the app's default macOS Application Support path is independent of shell `HOME`.
